sections.title: Handling the skill builder request
sections.what: Receives the profile and applications, counts skills and requirements, asks the AI for a skill-building result, and returns it or an error. It is the whole behaviour of this endpoint.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the AI call on the server so keys are not exposed. The code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: Applications with missing or oddly shaped fields can make the whole request fail.

summary: Server endpoint that counts the technical skills and key requirements across a user's tracked job applications and sends them, with the profile, to an AI model for a skill-building result.
purpose: Shows the user which skills keep appearing in the jobs they are targeting, so they can see what to build next.
why: Likely reason: the counting and the AI call run on the server, which keeps AI calls out of the browser. The code does not state this directly.
how: 1. Reads the profile and the list of applications from the request. 2. Returns a 400 error if no profile was sent. 3. Counts each technical skill across all applications, ignoring case and extra spaces. 4. Keeps up to three key requirements from each application. 5. Sorts skills from most to least common. 6. Sends the profile, the skill counts and up to 25 requirements to the AI with low randomness and a 4000-token output limit. 7. Returns the AI result under a data field. Any other failure returns a 500 error with a message.
inputs: A JSON body with profile (any shape) and applications (a list where each item may hold jdParsed with technicalSkills and keyRequirements).
outputs: On success, a JSON object with data holding the AI result. On failure, a JSON object with error and a 400 or 500 status.
risks: Applications are not checked for the expected shape, so one malformed entry fails the whole request. The profile is typed as any, so bad profile data is not caught here. The route does not pass the user's chosen AI provider, so it always uses the default provider.
debug: Open the browser network view and look at the response from /api/skill-builder. A 400 means the profile was missing from the request. A 500 with a message about a type or property usually means an application has an unexpected field shape. If every call fails, check the AI key in the server environment.
